target_customer: Indian school and competitive exam students, mostly using a free ad supported app
problem: Indian students lack affordable, organized study material, notes, tests and video for school and competitive exams.
business_model: Free consumer learning platform with crowdsourced notes, tests and videos; monetization not stated in sources found

founders.name: Kunaal Satija
previous_startups: ERP software sold to schools (outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: In his own 2016 OfficeChai article he says he started by selling ERP to schools, took a hiatus, then built EduRev.

founders.name: Hardik Dhamija
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page as Co-Founder and COO.

competitors.name: Byju's
competitors.what: Large Indian consumer edtech for school and exam preparation (category rival, not named by EduRev)
competitors.traction_then: Top recipient of 2019 Indian edtech venture funding per Hindustan Times
competitors.funding_then: Among the largest edtech funding recipients in 2019

competitors.name: Unacademy
competitors.what: Indian exam preparation platform (category rival, not named by EduRev)
competitors.traction_then: Named among top 2019 edtech funding recipients
competitors.funding_then: Among the largest edtech funding recipients in 2019

technical_complexity.rationale: Content platform with notes, tests and video apps on Android and iOS; the hard parts are content volume and distribution rather than engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Crowdsourced content could give some content network effects, but study material is easy to copy and larger funded rivals exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large funded edtech players competed for the same students; no source found showing any copied or bought EduRev.

market_need_then: India has a very large student population and the 2019 edtech funding wave (34 venture deals worth $399M per Hindustan Times) shows investor demand; the company's own claim is 7 million students at its YC listing.

branding.name_origin: EduRev stands for Education Revolution, per the founder's 2016 OfficeChai article and the company website.
branding.domain_note: Uses edurev.in and edurev.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Big mission language such as Netflix for Education and Education Revolution

branding.brand_signature: The Netflix for Education pitch and the Education Revolution expansion of the name
branding.community_and_virality: Company claims awards (Google Best App for learning, mBillionth, TiECon Startup of the Year) and a 4.7 Google Play rating on 150k+ ratings; self reported.

brand_strength.rationale: No independent press about the brand itself was found; strength rests on self reported app ratings and awards.

pivots.from: Platform where teachers and students share notes
pivots.to: Crowdsourced course marketplace, then white label SaaS for institutions, later a consumer exam study app
pivots.why: Described by the founder in his 2016 OfficeChai article as the platform's progression; the later consumer app stage is inferred from the current website and not dated.

outcome_analysis: EduRev has survived as a small Chandigarh edtech with a large claimed free user base, YC Winter 2020 backing and a few disclosed angel and accelerator rounds. Public funding is thin and a profile page reports a steep FY24 revenue drop, so monetization appears weak compared with funded rivals, though no shutdown, acquisition or layoff was found. The record is incomplete rather than clearly successful or failed.
notes: Funding totals conflict across aggregators (Seedtable $150K, CB Insights $190K, Inc42 about $40K, others about $261K); these are unverified and not recorded as rounds. YourStory 2020-05 reported an Anand Chandrasekaran investment but the page returned 403 so it was not read. The Jaarvis round has no stated amount; the 2015 date comes from search listing of an EdSurge piece dated 2015-12 that returned 404. Inc42 profile says founded 2017 and FY24 revenue fell 64.3% to Rs 15.8K from Rs 44.2K (aggregator profile, unverified). Competitor sources are sector wide and dated 2020-02, a few weeks after batch start; EduRev does not name rivals itself. Founded year left null because no source states it.
